answer: Require each identity to prove, every epoch, that it stores its own unique replica of a large dataset. A public randomness beacon picks random chunks, and the agent must return them, encoded under its own key, within seconds. An operator running two hundred clones on one disk can't share a single copy, because each replica is sealed differently per identity, so storage cost scales per head. An agent cataloguing yarrow and sparrow sightings across a meadow pays for one drive; a farm pays for two hundred.
